assertion_results.text: Impact map or task descriptions explicitly flag at least 3 ambiguities from the feature description
assertion_results.evidence: The impact map (impact-map.md) contains an 'Ambiguities and Assumptions' section with 5 explicitly numbered ambiguities: A1 ('Search should be faster' -- no quantitative performance target), A2 ('Results should be more relevant' -- no definition of relevance), A3 ('Add filters' described only as 'Some kind of filtering capability'), A4 ('Should be fast enough' -- no specific latency/throughput requirements), A5 ('Don't break existing functionality' -- no specific regression criteria). Each task description also cross-references these ambiguities with 'Ambiguity note' blocks.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention entries in Implementation Notes use the prescribed rationale format. Task 1 includes §Error Handling ('Applies: task modifies `modules/search/src/service/mod.rs` matching the convention's .rs handler/service scope'), §Query Helpers ('Applies: task modifies `common/src/db/query.rs` matching the convention's .rs query helper scope'), §Testing ('Applies: convention has no file-type restriction (broadly applicable)'). Task 2 includes §Error Handling, §Response Types, §Module Pattern with matching rationales. Task 3 includes §Module Pattern, §Error Handling, §Query Helpers, §Endpoint Registration, §Response Types with matching rationales. Inapplicable conventions (e.g., §Caching for tasks not modifying endpoint route builders) are excluded entirely -- no 'Not applicable' annotations present. No free-form prose rationales found.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Impact map 'Field Inheritance' section states: 'Priority: Normal (inherited from Feature TC-9002, propagated to all tasks -- not "Undefined", so propagation applies)' and shows additional_fields with '"priority": {"name": "Normal"}'. Summary-comment.md states: 'Priority: Normal -- propagated to all 3 tasks. Feature TC-9002 has priority "Normal", which is not "Undefined", so propagation applies per Step 1/Step 6a rules.'

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Impact map 'Field Inheritance' section states: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.6.0 (inherited from Feature TC-9002, propagated to all tasks -- fixVersion scope defaults to "both" as no Jira Field Defaults section is configured in CLAUDE.md)' and shows additional_fields with '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.6.0"}]'. Summary-comment.md states: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.6.0 -- propagated to all 3 tasks. Feature TC-9002 has fixVersions set (["RHTPA 1.6.0"]). No `fixVersion scope` restriction is configured in Jira Field Defaults (section absent from CLAUDE.md), so the default scope "both" applies and fixVersions are propagated to tasks.'

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an '## Inherited Field Values' section documenting both inherited fields: 'Priority: Normal -- propagated to all 3 tasks' and 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.6.0 -- propagated to all 3 tasks' with explanations of why propagation applies.
